BASIS OF PRESENTATION The Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements include the accounts of LCI Industries and its wholly-owned subsidiaries ("LCII" and collectively with its subsidiaries, the "Company," "we," "us," or "our"). LCII has no unconsolidated subsidiaries. All significant intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated. LCII, through its wholly-owned subsidiary, Lippert Components, Inc. and its subsidiaries (collectively, "Lippert Components," "LCI," or "Lippert"), is a global leader in supplying engineered components to the outdoor recreation, transportation, marine, and housing industries. In addition to serving original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs"), the Company also caters to aftermarket needs, selling through retail dealers, wholesale distributors, and service centers, as well as direct-to-consumer sales through online platforms. At September 30, 2026, the Company operated over 100 manufacturing facilities located throughout North America and Europe. The Company's results are influenced by seasonal demand patterns, with sales and profits typically strongest in the second quarter and weakest in the fourth quarter. However, economic conditions, dealer inventory fluctuations, and consumer trends can impact these patterns. Additionally, many of the optional upgrades and non-critical replacement parts for recreational vehicles ("RVs") are purchased outside the normal product selling season, thereby causing certain Aftermarket Segment sales to be counter-seasonal. The Company is not aware of any significant events which occurred subsequent to the balance sheet date but prior to the filing of this report that would have a material impact on the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements. In the opinion of management, the information furnished in this Form 10-Q reflects all adjustments necessary for a fair statement of the financial position and results of operations for the interim periods presented. Tariff Refunds In February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that certain tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA Tariffs") were not lawful. In March 2026, the Court of International Trade ("CIT") ordered U.S. Customs and Border Protection ("CBP") to begin the refund process for importers subject to IEEPA Tariffs, and in April 2026, CBP established an online portal through which importers may submit refund requests. The Company expects to receive $ 119.3 million in refunds, which represents the amount of IEEPA Tariffs the Company determined it paid while such tariffs were in effect from February 2025 through February 2026. The Company accounts for recoveries of previously incurred losses when realization is considered probable. The Company received $ 19.7 million and $ 114.6 million of IEEPA Tariff refunds during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively. The Company also received $ 0.7 million and $ 4.4 million of related interest income during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, which is included in interest expense, net in the Condensed Consolidated Statement of Income. Based on the status of the refund process and information currently available, the Company determined that recovery of the remaining IEEPA Tariffs previously paid was probable and recorded a receivable of $ 4.7 million at September 30, 2026, which is included in prepaid expenses and other current assets in the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized $ 104.8 million as a reduction of cost of sales, reflecting the reversal of IEEPA Tariff costs previously recognized in connection with inventory sold to customers. At September 30, 2026, the carrying value of inventory on hand includes a reduction of $ 4.8 million related to refunds of IEEPA Tariff costs previously recognized. The Company expects to pass through a portion of the IEEPA Tariff refunds received to certain customers. During each of the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company passed through $ 57.6 million of IEEPA Tariff refunds to certain customers. At September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a liability of $ 31.2 million, which is included in accrued expenses and other current liabilities in the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet, and reflects the remaining amount of IEEPA Tariff refunds that the Company expects to pass through to certain customers. The Company recorded a corresponding reduction to net sales of $ 88.8 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 related to the total amount of IEEPA Tariff refunds passed through or expected to be passed through to customers. The ultimate amount and timing of any remaining recovery and related payments to customers remain subject to uncertainty, including the outcome of the U.S. government’s appeal of the CIT order. Any changes in the estimated recovery or related customer pass-through obligations will be recognized in the period in which such changes are determined.
